bug.title: Deleting a todo while filtered removes the wrong item from the underlying list
observed_steps: 00:05 — User checks 'Buy milk' to mark it done
00:06 — User clicks the 'Active' filter button, showing 'Walk dog' and 'Pay rent'
00:07 — User clicks the delete ('×') button on 'Pay rent' (the second visible item in Active view)
bug.expected: Clicking delete on 'Pay rent' while in the 'Active' filter should delete 'Pay rent', leaving 'Buy milk' (done) and 'Walk dog' (active) when switching back to 'All'.
bug.actual: In the 'Active' view at 00:07, 'Walk dog' disappeared instead of 'Pay rent' (leaving only 'Pay rent' visible). Wait—actually at 00:07 'Pay rent' remains visible and 'Walk dog' is gone! And when switching to 'All' at 00:09, 'Buy milk' and 'Pay rent' are present while 'Walk dog' was deleted.
evidence_timestamps: 00:05 — 'Buy milk' is marked done (index 0 in todos), 'Walk dog' is index 1, 'Pay rent' is index 2
00:06 — 'Active' filter selected; visible items are 'Walk dog' (visible index 0) and 'Pay rent' (visible index 1)
00:07 — After clicking delete on 'Walk dog' or 'Pay rent', only 'Pay rent' remains in the Active list
00:09 — Switching back to 'All' shows 'Buy milk' and 'Pay rent'; 'Walk dog' (index 1 in the full todos array) was removed instead of the intended item
bug.root_cause_hypothesis: In `app/public/app.js`, `render()` iterates over the filtered array `visibleTodos()` with `items.forEach((t, i) => ...)` and binds the delete button click handler to `deleteTodo(i)` (line 88), passing the index `i` within the filtered `items` array rather than the todo's unique `t.id`. `deleteTodo(index)` (lines 47-52) then executes `todos.splice(index, 1)` on the unfiltered `todos` array. When a filter is active (e.g., 'Buy milk' at index 0 is done, so 'Active' shows 'Walk dog' at visible index 0 and 'Pay rent' at visible index 1), clicking delete on 'Pay rent' passes `i = 1`, causing `todos.splice(1, 1)` to delete 'Walk dog' instead of 'Pay rent' (or clicking delete on 'Walk dog' at `i = 0` would delete 'Buy milk'). `deleteTodo` should accept `id` and filter/find by `t.id` just like `toggleTodo(id)` does.

verdict.original_video_summary: The user added three todos ('Buy milk', 'Walk dog', 'Pay rent'), marked 'Buy milk' as done (00:05), switched to the 'Active' filter showing 'Walk dog' and 'Pay rent' (00:06), and clicked delete on 'Pay rent' (00:07). Instead of 'Pay rent' being deleted, 'Walk dog' disappeared leaving 'Pay rent' visible, and switching back to 'All' at 00:09 showed 'Buy milk' and 'Pay rent'.
verdict.fixed_video_summary: The automated test executed the reproduction steps (adding the three todos, marking 'Buy milk' done, switching to the 'Active' filter, and deleting 'Pay rent'). At 00:00 of the new recording, the 'Active' filter view correctly displays 'Walk dog' as the remaining active item after 'Pay rent' was deleted.
verdict.comparison: In the original recording at 00:07-00:08, under the 'Active' filter after deleting 'Pay rent', 'Walk dog' was erroneously removed and 'Pay rent' remained on screen. In the fixed build recording at 00:00, under the 'Active' filter, 'Pay rent' is gone and 'Walk dog' correctly remains on screen.
verdict.pr_description:
## Context
When viewing a filtered list of todos (e.g., `Active` or `Done`), clicking the delete (`×`) button on a todo item removed the wrong item from the underlying `todos` list.

## Root Cause
In `app/public/app.js`, `render()` iterated over the filtered `visibleTodos()` array (`items.forEach((t, i) => ...)`) and bound the delete click handler to `deleteTodo(i)`, passing the index within the filtered view rather than the todo's unique ID. `deleteTodo(index)` then called `todos.splice(index, 1)` on the unfiltered `todos` array, causing an index mismatch whenever any filter hid preceding items.

## Fix
- Updated `deleteTodo(id)` to accept the todo's unique `id` and filter `todos` via `todos = todos.filter(t => t.id !== id)`.
- Updated the delete button event listener in `render()` to call `deleteTodo(t.id)`.

## Verification
Verified with an automated Playwright test reproducing the customer scenario: adding 'Buy milk', 'Walk dog', and 'Pay rent', marking 'Buy milk' done, filtering by 'Active', and deleting 'Pay rent'. Confirmed that 'Pay rent' is removed while 'Walk dog' and 'Buy milk' remain intact.

rationale: In `app/public/app.js`, `render()` passed the index `i` from the filtered `visibleTodos()` list to `deleteTodo(index)`, which then spliced that index from the unfiltered `todos` array. When a filter like 'Active' or 'Done' hid items, the filtered index did not match the item's position in `todos`, causing the wrong todo to be deleted. Updating `deleteTodo` to accept the todo's unique `id` and passing `t.id` from the delete button click handler ensures the exact todo is removed regardless of the active filter.
